title: Rust: Hashing and Password Storage
description: Implement hashing algorithms and secure password storage concepts.

steps.title: Simple Hash Function
steps.description: Write a simple hash function `simple_hash(s: &str) -> u64` that sums the byte values and returns them mod 1000. Hash "hello" and "world" and print.
hints: This is NOT cryptographically secure — just for learning.

steps.title: Polynomial Rolling Hash
steps.description: Implement a polynomial rolling hash: `hash = Σ(s[i] * p^i) % m` where p=31, m=1_000_000_007. Hash "rust" and "tusr" (anagram) to show different hashes.
hints: `let mut h = 0u64; for (i, &b) in s.as_bytes().iter().enumerate() { h = h.wrapping_add((b as u64).wrapping_mul(P.pow(i as u32))); }`
This is the type of hash used in Rabin-Karp string matching.

steps.title: Hash Map from Scratch
steps.description: Implement a simple hash map with separate chaining (Vec of Vec of key-value pairs). Support `insert`, `get`, and `remove`. Test with several string→i32 mappings.
hints: `struct SimpleMap<K, V> { buckets: Vec<Vec<(K, V)>>, capacity: usize }`
`insert`: compute hash, find bucket, add or update entry.
`get`: find bucket, search for key, return value.

verification.failureMessage: Insert and retrieve values from your hash map.

steps.title: Password Hashing with Salt
steps.description: Write a function `hash_password(password: &str, salt: &str) -> String` that combines password and salt and returns a hash. Demonstrate that same password with different salts produces different hashes.
hints: `fn hash_password(pw: &str, salt: &str) -> String { format!("{:x}", simple_hash(&format!("{}{}", salt, pw))) }`
Same password + different salt = different hash.

verification.failureMessage: Hash passwords with different salts to show different results.

steps.title: Hash Collision Demo
steps.description: Find two strings that collide under `simple_hash` (same hash value mod 1000). Print both strings and their hash to demonstrate collisions.
hints: With mod 1000, collisions are guaranteed (pigeonhole principle).
Brute force: try different strings until collision found.
Or use a known collision: strings with same sum of byte values mod 1000.

verification.failureMessage: Find and print two strings that produce the same hash.
